findings.title: Organization slug logic inverted (unrelated change)
findings.body: The condition for setting the team `slug` was flipped from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. Now, when team billing is disabled (the default for self-hosted instances), the organization is created with no `slug` at all, so the org has no resolvable subdomain/URL; and when billing is enabled both `slug` and `metadata.requestedSlug` are written, which contradicts the "requested slug until paid" flow. This change is also unrelated to the destinationCalendar refactor and should be reverted.

findings.title: TypeError when Google Meet is selected and there is no destination calendar
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` can yield `undefined` (handleNewBooking explicitly sets `destinationCalendar: null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one). The next line dereferences it unconditionally: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`. For any booking with location `integrations:google:meet` and no destination calendar, this throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` and the whole booking creation fails. Use optional chaining (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`).

findings.title: Video booking references lose their credentialId
findings.body: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` replaces the previous `isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`. For video results (non-calendar) the credentialId coming from `createMeeting` is now discarded, so `BookingReference` rows for `*_video` are stored with `credentialId: null`. handleCancelBooking only deletes the meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so cancelling a booking will no longer delete the video meeting; other code paths that resolve the video credential from the reference are affected too. Keep `result.credentialId` for the non-calendar branch.

findings.title: updateEvent fallback calendar lookup is a no-op, yielding undefined calendarId
findings.body: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — the `find` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, and it compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e. against undefined/null), so it can never match. The previous code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Result: for any booking reference without `externalCalendarId` (legacy bookings, or references created by the new fallback paths that no longer set it), `calendar.events.update` is called with `calendarId: undefined`, so reschedules/updates fail. The fallback should be the first/matching destination calendar's `externalId`.

findings.title: deleteEvent fallback silently targets "primary" instead of the destination calendar
findings.body: Same broken lookup as in updateEvent: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can never match when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so `calendarId` becomes undefined and the code falls back to `"primary"`. Previously the destination calendar's `externalId` was used. When cancelling a booking whose reference lacks `externalCalendarId`, Google will return 404 for the event in `primary` (which the handler swallows), leaving the real event in the user's destination calendar undeleted and the slot blocked.

findings.title: hangoutLink patch uses possibly-undefined calendarId while insert used "primary"
findings.body: The insert call now uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` (used to rewrite the description with the Meet hangout link) still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. When no destination calendar matches the credential, `selectedCalendar` is undefined, the event was created in `primary`, and the patch request is made with an undefined calendarId — the description never gets the meeting link and the error is unhandled (fire-and-forget promise rejection).

findings.title: Destination calendars with a null credentialId now fall back to "primary"
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` is resolved only by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is nullable, and EventManager's new else-branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` (no externalId) for exactly those rows, so the find never matches and the event is created in `primary` instead of the configured destination calendar. Combined with `createEvent` being called without `externalId`, the resulting booking reference also has `externalCalendarId: undefined`, which then breaks subsequent update/delete (see the broken fallbacks in updateEvent/deleteEvent). Keep a fallback to the destination calendar's `externalId` when no credentialId match exists.

findings.title: Team hosts' destination calendars are dropped when there is no primary destination calendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` is a no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, which is exactly the case when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. In that situation a COLLECTIVE event with co-hosts who do have destination calendars will create no host calendar events at all (EventManager then falls into the `cred.type === "calendar"` legacy fallback, which never matches) — i.e. the bug this PR intends to fix is still present for that configuration. Build the array unconditionally (e.g. start from `[]` and push) instead of relying on optional chaining. Note also that when `eventType.destinationCalendar` is set, the organizer's personal calendar is intentionally excluded while every other host's personal calendar is added, which is an inconsistent semantic worth confirming.

findings.title: destinationCalendar payload shape is inconsistent (null vs [])
findings.body: handleNewBooking emits `destinationCalendar: null` when no calendar is configured, while every other producer changed in this PR (confirm.handler, handleCancelBooking, webhook.ts, paypal-webhook.ts, bookingReminder.ts, requestReschedule) emits `[]`. The field is forwarded verbatim to webhook subscribers (see apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts, which now expects `[]` for BOOKING_REJECTED but `null` for BOOKING_CREATED/BOOKING_REQUESTED). This is a breaking payload change for existing webhook/API consumers (object -> array) and it is not even internally consistent; pick one representation and document the breaking change.

findings.title: Dynamic-booking user query no longer selects `organization.slug`
findings.body: The rewritten `loadUsers` drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-group `prisma.user.findMany` select that existed before. Any downstream use of `user.organization?.slug` (e.g. computing booker/organization URLs) will now see `undefined` for dynamic bookings, and the two branches of `loadUsers` now return structurally different shapes, which also weakens/breaks the type inference the comment "loadUsers allows type inferring" relies on. Restore the selection or justify its removal.

findings.title: Stale `credential` reused across calendar references in updateAllCalendarEvents
findings.body: `credential` is declared once outside the new `for (const reference of calendarReference)` loop. If a reference has a `credentialId` that is neither in `this.calendarCredentials` nor resolvable from the DB (e.g. the credential row has no linked app slug), `credential` keeps the value from the previous iteration and `updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId)` is executed against the wrong account/credential — potentially writing one host's event into another host's calendar. On the first iteration it is `undefined`, which makes `updateEvent` throw. Declare `credential` inside the loop and skip the reference when it cannot be resolved.

findings.title: Error message in updateAllCalendarEvents is computed but never logged
findings.body: The catch block still builds the diagnostic `message` (including credential type, userId and bookingId) but the `console.error(message)` call was removed in this diff. Failures while updating calendar events now return `success: false` results with no trace in the logs, making reschedule/update failures undiagnosable.

findings.title: Recurring-event deletion is repeated once per calendar reference
findings.body: The recurring branch (iterating every user calendar credential × every updated booking reference) is now nested inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. With N calendar references on the booking, the same set of deleteEvent calls is issued N times, producing N× API calls to every calendar provider and repeated 404/410 responses. The recurring-cancellation block does not depend on `reference` at all and should be hoisted out of the per-reference loop.

findings.title: Non-Google calendar services still only read destinationCalendar[0], so secondary hosts get the wrong calendar
findings.body: EventManager now calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` once per destination with the *full* destinationCalendar array, but only GoogleCalendarService resolves the entry matching the credential. CalDAV/Apple (this file), Office365 (`createEvent`, line 73) and Lark (lines 128/164) destructure `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and therefore target the *first* host's external calendar id while authenticated as another host. In CalDAV this filters the calendar list down to zero entries, `Promise.all([])` resolves, `responses.some(r => !r.ok)` is false, and the method reports success although no event was created; Office365 builds `/me/calendars/<other host's id>/events` and 404s. These services receive the `credentialId` argument now and should use it (or the passed `externalId`) to pick the right destination entry.

findings.title: Calendar.createEvent second parameter made required
findings.body: `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)` makes `credentialId` mandatory on the public `Calendar` interface. Any caller outside `CalendarManager.createEvent` (including app-store calendar apps or external/consumer code implementing or invoking this interface) now fails type-checking, and most in-repo implementations ignore the parameter. Declaring it optional (`credentialId?: number`) would keep the contract backwards compatible.

findings.title: No tests for the new multi-destination-calendar behaviour
findings.body: This PR changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from a single object to an array across ~20 files and adds non-trivial branching (per-destination credential resolution with DB fallback, per-reference update/delete loops, collective host calendar aggregation) yet adds no unit/integration tests. The only test change is flipping one e2e expectation from `null` to `[]`, which leaves the other two webhook expectations asserting the old shape. Please add coverage for: collective event with two hosts each having a destination calendar, destination calendar rows with a null credentialId, and cancel/reschedule of a booking with multiple calendar references.
